themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 68 THIS WEEK—a 413% spike versus 13.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.02)—signaling rapid pavement or infrastructure degradation affecting multiple blocks in Sunset Park.
evidence: 68 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.2 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 11.02 indicates statistically extreme deviation
413% increase suggests sudden widespread pavement failure or pothole emergence
reporting_angles: Map 311 complaints by block to identify geographic hotspot and interview affected residents on commute/safety impact
Contact DOT to determine if weather events (freeze-thaw cycles, recent snow) triggered deterioration or if maintenance backlog is responsible

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Outbreak Signal
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints reached 3 THIS WEEK—a 700% spike from 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)—raising concern about potential restaurant sanitation failures or foodborne illness cluster in the district.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 5.42 indicates statistically significant spike
700% increase in single week warrants investigation of common source
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with Department of Health inspection records to identify which restaurants/vendors are implicated
Interview affected residents to confirm if complaints cluster around specific establishment or cuisine type

themes_detail.label: Construction Lead Dust Spike
themes_detail.summary: Construction lead dust complaints surged to 3 LAST WEEK—a 1100% spike from 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35)—indicating multiple renovation projects may be violating lead-safe work practices and exposing residents, especially children.
evidence: 3 lead dust complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 6.35 indicates extreme statistical deviation
581 building permits filed in last 90 days (417 alterations) suggests active renovation activity; correlate with lead complaints
1100% spike suggests systematic failure in lead safety compliance across multiple projects
reporting_angles: Identify which DOB-permitted alterations generated lead dust complaints; interview residents about respiratory symptoms or children's exposure
Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection to determine enforcement actions and whether contractors face penalties for RRP violations

themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/use violations jumped to 22 THIS WEEK—a 291% spike from 5.6 weekly average (z-score: 5.54)—suggesting illegal conversions, occupancy violations, or code enforcement failures across residential structures.
evidence: 22 building/use complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 5.54 indicates statistically significant spike
291% increase may indicate coordinated enforcement action or widespread illegal conversion activity
Aligns with long-standing CB budget requests for low-income housing—suggest displacement or unsafe conversions
reporting_angles: Query DOB violation database for specific addresses and violation types (illegal occupancy, SRO conversions, etc.)
Interview tenants at flagged buildings to determine if violations pose habitability risks or displacement threats

themes_detail.label: Maintenance and Facility Failures
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints spiked to 37 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 605% spike from 5.2 weekly average (z-score: 10.07)—indicating widespread deterioration of public infrastructure, transit stations, or municipal buildings.
evidence: 37 maintenance/facility complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 5.2 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 10.07 indicates extreme statistical deviation
605% spike suggests acute failure event affecting multiple city-maintained facilities
Aligns with recurring CB budget requests for park upgrades and transit improvements
reporting_angles: Identify whether spike is concentrated in parks, subway stations, NYCHA developments, or other facilities
Interview community board or elected officials about known maintenance crises; connect to unfunded capital requests
